title: Tomb of Askia, Gao
summary: The Tomb of Askia in Gao, Mali, is a stepped pyramidal tomb of mud brick, about 17 m high, built in 1495 by Askia Mohamed, emperor of the Songhai Empire. It stands with two flat-roofed mosques, a cemetery and an open assembly ground within a walled enclosure. Timbers projecting from its face serve as permanent scaffolding for the regular replastering.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO and ICOMOS both say the tomb was built in 1495. End is the present: the site stands and is maintained by regular replastering.

reviewer_note: Shape stepped_pyramid: ICOMOS calls it a 'large stepped, pyramidal tomb' (no tier count is given, so none is recorded). UNESCO's page prints the coordinate N16 17 23.28, E0 2 40.416 (about 16.2898, 0.0446); the OSM point is at the same distance from the prime meridian but on the west side (-0.0449), and the OSM sign is used. Both are within about 0.1 km if the UNESCO longitude is read as west. Least sure of the UNESCO longitude sign.
